Subject: MAP kickoff + timeline for deployment venue and region binding

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood yesterday — the demo was helpful. Our execs want to lock the deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and pick the primary region before the end of May so procurement can start cloud approvals.

Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation steps, acceptance gates, and a recommended timeline? Key constraints from our side:
- Data residency requirement: primary processing must be in US-East (we have legacy data in us-east-1).
- Expected QPS: peak ~1200 reqs/min for triage model.
- Security: need SOC2 evidence and an initial data flow diagram for our security review.

If possible, include a short decision matrix that maps risk/cost/latency tradeoffs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Attaching a short internal checklist we used in our intake.

Thanks,
Claire
Senior PM, Nimbus Health

Hi Claire (and Peter),

Appreciate the clarity — this is exactly the kind of input we need. I've attached a working MAP template and an evaluation checklist that maps the acceptance gates to ownership and estimated lead times. High level proposal below:

Proposed MAP highlights (summary):
- Week 1 (May 4–8): Discovery deep-dive (security questionnaire, data flow, and SLA needs).
- Week 2 (May 11–15): Proof-of-concept (PoC) in Hosted with sample traffic + latency baseline in us-east.
- Week 3 (May 18–22): Dedicated sizing exercise if procurement prefers reserved capacity; parallel private feasibility if on-prem considered.
- Week 4 (May 25–29): Decision gating — run cost/latency matrix, finalize region pin, and sign-off to start procurement.

Quick notes on tradeoffs:
- Hosted: fastest onboarding, easiest for a May baseline. Cost-effective for bursty workloads but less isolation.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and isolation; requires procurement lead time (2–4 weeks for contract + capacity reservation).
- Private: only for strict regulatory needs; longer timeline (estimated 6–10 weeks) and heavier ops.

I've looped Priya (AE) to coordinate procurement cadence and Rishi (SA) will follow with a technical appendix — he has latency and KV-cache sizing estimates. Attaching: Nimbus_MAP_v1.3.xlsx and evaluation_checklist_0504.pdf.

Next steps:
1) Claire: confirm the data residency constraint (US-East only?) and whether temporary Hosted PoC in us-east is acceptable.
2) Nimbus: share security questionnaire responses by May 7.
3) Redwood: Rishi to provide latency/cost delta for Hosted vs Dedicated in us-east by EOD May 5.

Best,
Soojin
Senior GTM Strategist, Redwood Inference

Hi team,

Posting the technical appendix requested. Key items from our initial sizing and latency runs (summary):
- Baseline PoC in Hosted (us-east-1) with sample payloads: median token-latency ~65ms, p95 ~240ms at ~300 concurrent sessions.
- For target peak (1200 reqs/min), continuous batching and prefix caching expected to keep p95 under 350ms on the Hosted tier for the medium-sized model we demoed.
- Dedicated sizing: a 2x T4 pool (or single A10x-based pool) gives headroom for sustained throughput with p95 <200ms but requires reserved capacity.
- Private/on-prem: network egress and data ingestion cost/time varies by customer infra; added ~2–3 weeks to provisioning for VPN/KMS integration.

Attachments: redwood-region-latency-estimates.csv (latency by region and model), and a brief config diff that maps PoC config to Dedicated config.

Recommendation for MAP gating:
- Gate 1 (security check): SOC2 docs & data flow diagram — must be clear before PoC.
- Gate 2 (PoC baseline): Hosted PoC metrics meet latency threshold (p95 <350ms).
- Gate 3 (procurement): If opting Dedicated, procurement commit + capacity reservation completed.

I'll be available for a short call May 6 to walk through the CSV and sizing numbers.

-Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
